compare-four-methods.description: The same face pair, with points and lines. Compare eyes and mouth halfway through.
compare-four-methods.name: Compare — four algorithms

crossfade-reference.description: No landmarks: observe the double contours, then try the comparison.
crossfade-reference.name: Crossfade — see ghosting

faces-points-tps.description: Move a point, show the TPS grid and compare with border anchors disabled.
faces-points-tps.name: Claire → Bunny — TPS landmarks

faces-lines-beier.description: Oriented lines on eyes, nose and mouth. Adjust their a, b, p influence.
faces-lines-beier.name: Faces — Beier–Neely lines

cars-mesh.description: Wheels and silhouette guide the triangles. Show the mesh to read the deformation.
cars-mesh.name: Cars — mesh

layer-full-frame.description: Hide the top layer: without a mask it replaces the entire Global image.
layer-full-frame.name: Layer — full frame

layer-region-mask.description: TPS on the face, crossfade around it. Inspect Mask and Contribution; adjust the outline and feather.
layer-region-mask.name: Region — one algorithm per area

mask-invert-blend.description: The mask protects the face. Toggle the layer to see Multiply at 40% opacity.
mask-invert-blend.name: Inverted mask — Multiply

blend-light.description: Two layers brighten the image: Screen on the face and Add (Lighter) around it. View each layer on its own and adjust its opacity.
blend-light.name: Blend — Screen and Lighter

painted-mask.description: The mask painted on A follows TPS. Inspect Mask at 25, 50 and 75%, then try the brush and eraser.
painted-mask.name: Painted mask — follow the morph

combined-masks.description: The hard-edged region adds to the painted mask (union). Inspect Mask, then try the eraser outside the region.
combined-masks.name: Combined masks — region and brush

contours-push.description: Select Push (K), reshape a cheek, then undo. Close a copy of the contour to explore polygons.
contours-push.name: Contours — sculpt with Push

transition-classic.description: Compare Standard and Classic morph: warp 0–100%, dissolve 30–70%. Watch the beginning and end.
transition-classic.name: Transition — classic morph

layers-timing.description: The face dissolves before the hair. Separate windows and a Bézier; layers remain visible to the end.
layers-timing.name: Timing — face then surroundings

fruits-banana-pineapple.description: A closed outline animated on still images. Move the diamonds, then play ping-pong.
fruits-banana-pineapple.name: Fruit — keyframes and ping-pong

fruit-to-fox.description: The crown becomes ears and the fruit becomes a face. Paired silhouettes, without human facial landmarks.
fruit-to-fox.name: Pineapple → Foxy — metamorphosis

transparent-cutout.description: 4:3 images in a square canvas: the margins are transparent. Export PNG frames with Transparent background; video flattens the background.
transparent-cutout.name: Export — transparent canvas

video-faces-keyframes.description: 44 landmarks tracked on every frame: eyes, nose, lips and jaw. Clip B is trimmed to bring the expressions closer.
video-faces-keyframes.name: Video — landmarks and keyframes

video-region-keyframes.description: The outline and mouth line follow every frame. Inspect the mask, then select the line and its keyframes.
video-region-keyframes.name: Video — animated mask and line

video-photo-alive.description: The photo becomes a video of the same face in one second. Only side B has keyframes; A landmarks stay fixed.
video-photo-alive.name: Photo → video — come alive

video-clips-timing.description: A: 0–3 s, B: 1.5–4.5 s. Landmarks follow media time through trims; the morph spans their overlap.
video-clips-timing.name: Clips — trim and overlap

video-body-walk.description: 16 landmarks per frame. Detected pose on the officer; manual anchors and optical flow on the robot. The layer acts during the overlap.
video-body-walk.name: Walking — full-body morph

about.description: A WebGPU & WebCodecs studio for 2D image and video morphing.
about.author: Created by André Frélicot.
about.privacy: Your images, videos and projects are processed on your device. Rendering and export run in your browser, without uploading your media to a server.

loadImagesGuide.title: Load two images
loadImagesGuide.description: Fill Source A and Target B — demo assets or your own files.
loadImagesGuide.keywords: load import images demo assets presets example source target open file

demo.title: Start with the demo assets
demo.body:
Demo → Presets opens a teaching catalog. Each card shows its source/target pair and an exercise. Start with Compare — four algorithms, then explore masks, transitions, keyframes and video. Examples open at an authored time, with the useful view and layer selected. Landmark names stay in English in every interface language.

These presets are automatically generated to demonstrate the studio’s features. Artistic results are not guaranteed.

source.title: Or import your own — Source A
source.body: This slot accepts an image or a video file: it is the morph's starting side.

target.title: Target B
target.body: Fill the second slot — as soon as both sides exist the project is created and the preview renders.

chooseAlgorithmGuide.title: Choose the morphing algorithm
chooseAlgorithmGuide.description: Pick the project algorithm and understand the four families.
chooseAlgorithmGuide.keywords: algorithm crossfade mesh tps thin-plate spline beier neely warp
chooseAlgorithmGuide.preconditionHint: Load two images first — the Demo button in the top bar is the fastest way.

algorithm-list.title: The four algorithms
algorithm-list.body: Crossfade dissolves without warping. Mesh warps Delaunay triangles. Thin-Plate Spline bends the whole image smoothly. Beier–Neely warps along oriented lines.
algorithm-list.missingHint: Open the Studio tab and the Algorithm section.

pick-tps.title: Try Thin-Plate Spline
pick-tps.body: Click the Thin-Plate Spline tile — the preview re-renders instantly with the new warp.
pick-tps.missingHint: Open the Studio tab and the Algorithm section.

settings.title: Algorithm settings
settings.body: The active algorithm's settings appear right below the tiles — for TPS, the λ slider trades exactness for smoothness.
settings.missingHint: Pick TPS or Beier–Neely to reveal their settings.

navigateViewsGuide.title: Navigate the studio views
navigateViewsGuide.description: Edit, Preview and Triple; zoom, pan and reset the viewport.
navigateViewsGuide.keywords: view edit preview triple zoom pan reset navigate viewport
navigateViewsGuide.preconditionHint: Load two images first — the Demo button in the top bar is the fastest way.

toggle.title: Three views
toggle.body: Edit shows A | B for placing features, Preview shows the morph full-size, Triple shows A | morph | B. On narrow views, choose the view from the menu.

triple.title: Open the Triple view
triple.body: Click Triple — you edit on the sides while the center morphs live. When the preview pane is narrow, open Preview controls to choose Final, Layer, Mask or Contribution, show overlays or inspect the layer stack.

zoom-pan.title: Zoom, pan, reset
zoom-pan.body: Scroll or pinch to zoom. Hold Space or select the Pan tool (H), then drag to pan. Double-click or double-tap to reset the viewport. On touch devices, the workspace stays fixed; only sheets and panels scroll.
zoom-pan.missingHint: Open the Studio tab in Edit or Triple view.

saveLoadGuide.title: Save and reload a project
saveLoadGuide.description: Save project structure and embedded images; relink local videos after reopening.
saveLoadGuide.keywords: save load project file morph json export reopen
saveLoadGuide.preconditionHint: Load two images first — the Demo button in the top bar is the fastest way.

save.title: Save
save.body: Save downloads a .morph.json with embedded images, features, layers and timeline. Video bytes stay local and are referenced by metadata — nothing leaves your machine.

load.title: Load it back
load.body: Load restores the project structure and embedded images. For each local video, use Relink on its A/B slot; playback and export resume once all required files are connected.

aboutGuide.title: Credits
aboutGuide.description: Credits, app version and local media processing.

about.title: Open About
about.body: About in the top bar shows the author, the build version and how your media stays on your device. On the compact layout, look in More.
about.missingHint: Leave zen mode or open the More menu to find About.

languageGuide.title: Change the interface language
languageGuide.description: Choose a language for the studio, examples and guides.
languageGuide.body: Open the language selector in the top bar. Each card shows a flag and the language’s native name. Your choice is remembered on this device. Wait for loading to finish before the interface changes. A connection may be needed to download a language’s fonts. Your project and landmark names stay unchanged. If a saved language cannot be restored, the app opens in English with an explanation and a retry button. On narrower screens, the top bar can wrap onto multiple rows to keep all commands visible.

needsProject.preconditionHint: Load two images first — the Demo button in the top bar is the fastest way.

features.studioHint: Open the Studio tab in Edit view.

placePointsGuide.title: Place correspondence points
placePointsGuide.description: Points tell Mesh and TPS which spot of A matches which spot of B.
placePointsGuide.keywords: point landmark correspondence mesh tps place adjust

place-a.title: Click a landmark on A
place-a.body: Click a distinctive spot (an eye, a corner…) in the Source A pane. A matching handle appears on B.

adjust-b.title: Adjust side B
adjust-b.body: Drag the twin handle in Target B onto the same landmark of the other image — that pairing drives the warp.

preview.title: Watch the warp
preview.body: Switch to Preview or Triple to see Mesh/TPS bend the images through your points.

drawLinesGuide.title: Draw oriented lines (Beier–Neely)
drawLinesGuide.description: Line pairs drive the Beier–Neely field morphing.
drawLinesGuide.keywords: line segment oriented beier neely edge draw

drag-line.title: Drag along an edge on A
drag-line.body: Press and drag to lay a line along a strong edge (jawline, roofline…). Its twin appears on B.

orient-b.title: Match the direction on B
orient-b.body: Move both endpoints on B onto the same edge, keeping the SAME direction — Beier–Neely maps along and across each line.

use-beier.title: Switch to Beier–Neely
use-beier.body: Lines only warp with the Beier–Neely algorithm — pick its tile.
use-beier.missingHint: Open the Studio tab and the Algorithm section.

drawPolylineGuide.title: Draw a polyline
drawPolylineGuide.description: Tap-by-tap or freehand curves, resumable from an endpoint.
drawPolylineGuide.keywords: polyline curve path freehand tap draw resume endpoint

tap-by-tap.title: Tap by tap
tap-by-tap.body: Click successive points along a contour. Press ⏎ to finish, Esc to cancel.

freehand.title: Or freehand
freehand.body: Press and drag in one continuous stroke — the path is simplified automatically on release.

resume.title: Resume from an endpoint
resume.body: With the Polyline tool active, click an endpoint of an open polyline to keep drawing from there.

closePolygonGuide.title: Close an open polyline
closePolygonGuide.description: Two ways to turn an open polyline into a closed polygon.
closePolygonGuide.keywords: close polygon polyline loop endpoint drop first point

intro.title: Two ways to close
intro.body: A polyline can be closed while you draft it, or later with the Select tool.

close-first.title: While drafting: click point 1
close-first.body: While drawing, click the FIRST point again — the loop closes and the draft finishes.

drop-endpoint.title: Later: endpoint onto endpoint
drop-endpoint.body: With the Select tool, drag one endpoint of an open polyline and drop it on the other endpoint — same result.

drawRegionGuide.title: Draw a region
drawRegionGuide.description: A closed region can mask a layer; adjust the softness of its edge.
drawRegionGuide.keywords: region mask lasso outline feather draw

pick-tool.title: The Region mask tool
pick-tool.body: Select the Region mask tool — its contour is always closed.

outline.title: Outline the area on A
outline.body: Tap points or draw freehand around the area (a face, an object). Finish with ⏎ or by closing the loop.

feather.title: Feather the edge
feather.body: Select the region and adjust Feather to soften its edge. A layer using this region as a mask also has its own mask mode and feather setting.
feather.missingHint: Open the Selection section of the right inspector.

manageSelectionGuide.title: Select, rename, lock, hide
manageSelectionGuide.description: Manage features and read the A↔B hover beacon.
manageSelectionGuide.keywords: select multi-select shift rename lock hide beacon hover feature

select.title: Click a handle
select.body: Click a feature handle to select it — hold Shift to multi-select. Hovering shows a beacon on the matching handle in the OTHER pane.

inspector.title: Rename, lock, hide
inspector.body: The Selection section renames the feature and toggles Visible / Locked.
inspector.missingHint: Open the Selection section of the right inspector.

list.title: The Features list
list.body: The left list mirrors everything: eye hides, padlock locks, and clicking selects.

pushPointsGuide.title: Push points & undo
pushPointsGuide.description: Sculpt handles locally with the Push tool; undo/redo any step.
pushPointsGuide.keywords: push sculpt deform local radius undo redo

sculpt.title: Drag to sculpt
sculpt.body: Drag across the image: every handle inside the ring is pushed along, strongest at the center.

undo.title: Undo / redo
undo.body: Cmd/Ctrl+Z undoes any feature edit; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes it.

layers.layersHint: Open the Layers section of the right inspector.

needsProject.preconditionHint: Load two images first — the Demo button in the top bar is the fastest way.

activateLayerStep.title: Activate a user layer
activateLayerStep.body: Click a layer other than Global in the Layers section — its properties appear right below the list.

createLayerGuide.title: Create a layer
createLayerGuide.description: Stack layers above the Global base and read their contribution badges.
createLayerGuide.keywords: layer create add stack global order badge contribution

add.title: Add a layer
add.body: Click Add layer — the new layer becomes active immediately.

global-vs-layers.title: Global vs user layers
global-vs-layers.body: Global renders the default morph underneath. User layers composite above it, in list order — the arrows reorder the stack.

badges.title: Contribution badges
badges.body: Each row shows what the layer does right now: full frame (covers everything), masked, no contribution, outside clip…

layerOverrideGuide.title: Change a layer's algorithm
layerOverrideGuide.description: Give one layer its own algorithm without touching the project default.
layerOverrideGuide.keywords: layer algorithm override mesh tps beier per-layer

override.title: Pick an override
override.body: The Algorithm dropdown in the layer properties replaces the project default for THIS layer only.

badge.title: The override badge
badge.body: The Algorithm section header now shows an override badge — and everything stays reachable even with a feature selected.
badge.missingHint: Open the Algorithm section of the right inspector.

maskRegionGuide.title: Mask a layer with a region
maskRegionGuide.description: Restrict a layer to an assigned region, hard or feathered, invertible.
maskRegionGuide.keywords: mask region assign layer hard feathered invert
maskRegionGuide.preconditionHint: Draw a region first (Region mask tool) — the mask dropdown lists regions.

assign.title: Assign a region
assign.body: Pick a region in the Mask dropdown: the layer now composites only inside it.

modes.title: Hard, feathered, inverted
modes.body: Mask mode switches between a hard cut and a feathered edge (with its own feather value); Invert flips inside/outside.

paintMaskGuide.title: Paint a mask
paintMaskGuide.description: Brush a mask directly on the image, watch it live in the preview.
paintMaskGuide.keywords: paint brush mask diameter hardness strength eraser clear live

pick-brush.title: The Mask brush
pick-brush.body: Select the Mask brush (shortcut B) — it paints the ACTIVE layer's mask.

settings.title: Brush settings
settings.body: Diameter, hardness and strength shape the stroke. Eraser removes paint — tick the box or hold ⌥ while dragging.
settings.missingHint: The settings appear under the tool grid while the brush is active.

paint.title: Paint on the image
paint.body: Drag on a pane: the painted mask composites LIVE in the central preview (see the Final and Mask debug views). The paint is advected with the layer's warp, so it follows the content as it morphs.
paint.missingHint: Open the Studio tab in Edit view.

clear.title: Clear it anytime
clear.body: Painted mask → Clear resets the layer's painted mask entirely.

layerLookGuide.title: Opacity, blend, clip and transition
layerLookGuide.description: Adjust a layer’s appearance, limit its time on the timeline, and choose when it dissolves.
layerLookGuide.keywords: opacity blend mode composite clip timeline start duration easing transition warp dissolve window preset classic morph bezier curve ghosting

opacity.title: Opacity
opacity.body: Slide the opacity below 1 to blend the layer with what is underneath.

blend.title: Blend mode
blend.body: The Blend menu controls how the layer combines with those underneath: Normal, Multiply, Screen or Add (Lighter). Multiply multiplies colors; Screen brightens them; Add sums premultiplied colors and alpha, clamping the result to the maximum value.

clip.title: Clip it in time
clip.body: Drag the layer's block in the timeline to move it, its edges to trim it — or set Start and Duration in the layer properties.

windows.title: Warp long, dissolve short
windows.body: The Transition section defines two windows as percentages of the clip. Warp controls the change of shape; Dissolve controls the blend between images A and B. The Classic morph preset keeps Warp at 0–100% and limits Dissolve to 30–70%. This reduces ghosting from poorly aligned details at the beginning and end.

windows-timeline.title: Read the windows in the timeline
windows-timeline.body: The layer's block draws both windows along its bottom edge: a light band for the dissolve, a hairline for the warp. You see at a glance where in the clip the crossfade happens.

easing.title: Shape the curve
easing.body: Easing sets the rhythm of both windows: five named curves, or “custom (bezier)” for a two-handle CSS-style curve you drag. Tick “Distinct dissolve curve” to give the crossfade its own rhythm, independent of the warp.

global-too.title: The Global layer too
global-too.body: Select Global: it has the same Transition section. Its windows cover 0–100% by default. With Crossfade, only the dissolve window has an effect because this algorithm does not deform the images.

needsProject.preconditionHint: Load two images first — the Demo button in the top bar is the fastest way.

timelineGuide.title: Drive the timeline
timelineGuide.description: Scrub, play, step frames and move layer clips.
timelineGuide.keywords: timeline scrub play pause frame timecode clip move trim zen tab collapse panels ruler playhead

scrub.title: Scrub the ruler
scrub.body: Click or drag anywhere on the ruler — τ follows and the preview seeks that exact frame. With a stylus, touch any position and keep the tip down while dragging.

transport.title: Play, pause, step
transport.body: Play runs the morph in real time. The arrow buttons (or ←/→) step one frame; Alt-click jumps to the ends. The timecode reads seconds:frames.

clips.title: Move and trim clips
clips.body: Images and videos have clips on A/B, above the layer clips. Drag a block or resize its edges; selecting it exposes Start and Duration. A still image has no source-length limit: increasing its duration can extend the montage. Outside a media clip only the other side contributes; if neither is present, the background is shown.

still-image-timing.title: Time a still image
still-image-timing.body: Select an image clip on A or B and enter its duration in seconds (or seconds:frames). Shortening a clip leaves the montage duration unchanged; extending it grows the timeline when needed. Still-image landmark keys keep their master times: moving or resizing the clip does not move or stretch their animation. Clips are saved with the project.

zen.title: Zen mode keeps the ruler
zen.body: {{shortcut}} hides all three panels so the morph fills the screen. The timeline collapses to a single 40 px bar that still carries a compact ruler: ticks, timecodes and the playhead — and you can still click or drag it to scrub. Press {{shortcut}} again to bring the panels back.

videosGuide.title: Morph between videos
videosGuide.description: Import videos, place the A/B clips and add feature keyframes.
videosGuide.keywords: video clip import keyframe pose track sing diamond drag retime

get-videos.title: Get two videos
get-videos.body: The Demo dialog ships four singing clips and two walking clips (filter: Videos) — or drop your own video files on the A/B slots. Mixing an image with a video works too. Saved projects keep video metadata and ask you to relink the local files when reopened.

place-clips.title: Place the A/B clips
place-clips.body: Each video lives on its track: drag to move, edges to trim, and the start/in/dur fields for exact values. Moving or trimming a clip refreshes the preview at the playhead, without having to move the playhead itself; the montage duration stays unchanged. Landmark keyframes stay tied to source-media time, including the trimmed-in portion, and are preserved when saving and reopening. Outside its clip that side is excluded from both preview and export; the other side fills the frame.

keyframes.title: Add feature keyframes
keyframes.body: Select a feature: the Keyframes row has, per side, previous ◀, a diamond ◆ that adds or removes a keyframe at the current time, next ▶, and the count. Features then track the motion between keyframes. On still images a feature stays static until you add a first keyframe with ◆ — after that, moves at other times add keyframes and bend the morph path.
keyframes.missingHint: Open the Selection section of the right inspector.

timeline-keyframes.title: Edit keyframes on the timeline
timeline-keyframes.body: The selected features' keyframes show as diamonds on the A and B tracks, at the time they play. Click one to jump there, drag it to retime it (frame-snapped, one undo step), Alt-click to delete it. Diamonds too close to tell apart merge into a bar with a count — use the inspector arrows to reach them.

compareGuide.title: Compare the algorithms
compareGuide.description: See all four algorithms side by side on the same project.
compareGuide.keywords: compare grid side by side crossfade mesh tps beier

open.title: Open Compare
open.body: The Compare tab renders a 2×2 grid sharing your images, features and τ.

read.title: Read the grid
read.body: Crossfade produces double contours where image details are misaligned. Mesh, TPS and Beier–Neely warp both images toward a shared intermediate shape to align corresponding details.

exportGuide.title: Export MP4 or frames
exportGuide.description: Render the morph to a video file or a ZIP of PNG frames.
exportGuide.keywords: export mp4 webm av1 zip frames video render download

open.title: Open Export
open.body: Everything renders locally — nothing is uploaded.

settings.title: Pick the output
settings.body: Video needs WebCodecs and an available H.264, VP9 or AV1 encoder. The PNG image sequence needs no video codecs and can preserve a transparent background. Video is flattened onto black or white. Set the resolution, duration and frame rate.

run.title: Export
run.body: The morph renders frame by frame with a progress bar, then the file downloads automatically. The same button cancels safely while an export is running.

shortcutsGuide.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcutsGuide.description: Every shortcut, straight from the app's shortcut tables.
